suppress.notes:
FALSE POSITIVE. Dependency-Check matches io.projectreactor.netty:reactor-netty-core to cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty by version number alone (1.2.18), and then attaches the entire Netty advisory history to it -- 64 CVEs per service, including CVE-2019-20444/20445 and the netty-codec-http request-smuggling family. The report itself marks the match as low confidence. reactor-netty is a separate Spring project artifact and is not the software those advisories describe.
Scoped to the reactor-netty-core jar by file path on purpose: the real io.netty:* jars it pulls in are NOT suppressed and must keep reporting. Those are pinned via <netty.version> in each pom (4.1.137.Final at the time of writing).
SCOPE NARROWED 2026-08-31: only mas-api-gateway still ships reactor-netty. NDI never used its webflux starter at all (removed), and Quarrying-Lease now runs WebClient on JdkClientHttpConnector with spring-boot-starter-reactor-netty excluded, so the jar is gone from both. The gateway cannot follow them: Spring Cloud Gateway's WebSocketClient bean comes from NettyConfiguration, and without it the context fails to start outright (verified - filteringWebHandler -> websocketRoutingFilter -> no WebSocketClient bean). This rule is kept in the other repos as a safety net in case a webflux starter returns transitively; it currently matches nothing there, which is the intended state.

FALSE POSITIVE. CVE-2018-1258 is an authorization bypass affecting Spring Security 5.0.5 used together with Spring Framework 5.0.5, fixed in 5.0.6 in 2018. The NVD entry carries an open-ended version range, so Dependency-Check re-flags it against every later release indefinitely. Nothing in MAS runs an affected version -- the estate is on Spring Security 6.5.x (Boot 3.5) and 7.0.x (Boot 4.0).
Affects all nine backends: core, web, oauth2-resource-server and crypto jars.

NOT APPLICABLE / NO OSS FIX AVAILABLE. Two Spring Framework advisories published 2026-08-20 against spring-core 6.2.0 - 6.2.19. Both are rated LOW by VMware in their own advisories; NVD's 9.8 CRITICAL score on CVE-2026-59313 is an NVD scoring artifact, not the maintainer's assessment.
CVE-2026-59313 (SSE stream corruption) requires ALL of: the MVC functional web framework (RouterFunction / ServerResponse.sse()), Server-Sent Events streaming, attacker-controlled stream content, and plain-text (non-JSON) messages. MAS uses none of it -- RouterFunction, ServerResponse.sse, SseEmitter and text/event-stream have ZERO occurrences across every backend in the estate. Re-verify that grep each round.
CVE-2026-59314 (ContentDisposition response splitting) is blocked twice over here: every service runs on Tomcat, which the advisory states already rejects CR/LF in header values, and the three ContentDisposition call sites in the estate (mas-backend-masters PublicWebsiteController, mas-file-upload DocumentController, MiningLease RenewalEnvironmentalClearanceController) all now use the filename(name, Charset) overload, which emits the RFC 5987 filename* form and percent-encodes CR/LF. The outbound-multipart case does not exist in this codebase.
WHY NOT SIMPLY UPGRADE: the fix for the 6.2.x line is 6.2.20, which VMware ships as "Enterprise Support Only" -- it is not on Maven Central. 6.2.19 is the last OSS release of that line (2026-06-08), as 3.5.16 is the last OSS Spring Boot 3.5 release (2026-06-25). The only OSS fix is Spring Framework 7.0.9, i.e. a Spring Boot 3.5 -> 4.0 major migration, tracked separately. mas-backend-report already runs Boot 4.0.8 / spring-core 7.0.9 and does NOT report these.
Scoped to spring-core 6.2.x by file path on purpose: it stops matching the moment a service moves to the Boot 4 / spring-core 7.0.9+ line, so the rule expires by itself rather than masking a future finding.

See the CVE-2026-59313 entry above -- same advisory batch, same reasoning, same scoping. CVE-2026-59314 is ContentDisposition response splitting; LOW (3.7), blocked by the Tomcat connector and by the RFC 5987 filename* encoding now used at every ContentDisposition call site in the estate. Fixed in 6.2.20 (Enterprise Support Only) or 7.0.9 (OSS, Boot 4).
